claims.claim_en: THE CALENDAR THESIS resolves the unit's two [OPEN] grammar flags JOINTLY: yehi ('let there be', qal jussive SINGULAR, Vqj3ms) over me'orot ('lights', PLURAL) + the doubly-defective spelling מארת ('luminaries', written lean) are read together by the chain — 'only the sun-orb was created to illuminate; why then the moon? to sanctify New Moons and years by its calculation' (R. Yochanan, with the written-form argument explicit in Pesikta DeRav Kahana: 'ME'OROT IS WRITTEN'). One illuminator, one calendar instrument. R. Shilo adds: months counted only once the sun has set.
claims.middah_note: letter-form derivation from the defective written skeleton (the ktiv, 'what is written') — the al-tiqrei family; not cleanly one of the 32 as cataloged in logic/MIDDOT.md, honestly left unnumbered
claims.mechanics: both [OPEN] flags (number mismatch; three orthographies) close to CHAIN-WITNESSED — the day-one C9 precedent: the machine facts stand as facts of the text, the chain's joint resolution is recorded beside them on the 1:14 DECLARE. No state change; flag-status change only.

claims.claim_en: The SAME defective skeleton carries a second chain derivation: מארת read as מארה ('curse') — 'on the fourth day they would fast for the children, that askara (diphtheria) not rise in their mouths… ME'OROT IS WRITTEN' — the Wednesday fast of the ma'amadot (the standing-watches liturgy) hung on our token. One written form, two derivations (calendar thesis + curse reading), both chain-primary.
claims.mechanics: witness-tier note attached to the orthography flag: the lean spelling is LOAD-BEARING twice over. No machine state; the fast is Israel-side practice, out of span.

claims.claim_en: ANTI-DEIFICATION RATIONALE, argued by explicit a-fortiori: R. Zeira — 'if two that contradict each other are deified — one alone, ALL THE MORE SO' (had only one luminary been made, it would surely be worshipped): the differentiation and the roughness of the grammar carry a design rationale against worship of the fixtures. Bereshit Rabbati adds the same rationale for the unequal hours ('so that the me'orot not be thought gods').
claims.middah_note: explicit qal wa-chomer ('light and heavy', a-fortiori) at narrative strength — the middah named per Step 5
claims.mechanics: witness-tier rationale note on the DECLARE; no operator, no state. The middah's constraint (conclusion may not exceed premise — the dayo cap) is not strained: the conclusion stays within worship-risk.

claims.claim_en: THE SECOND HANDOVER: the tannaitic reading of our job list — 'the commandments given to them FROM THE HEAVENS: intercalation of years and fixing of New Moons, as it is stated: ve-hayu le-otot u-le-mo'adim ('and they shall be for signs and for appointed times')' — the calendar job is delegated not only TO the fixtures but onward THROUGH them, as Israel's computational duty. Day 4 already holds the corpus's first operational handover (machine → fixtures, the divide function); the Sifrei adds a second leg: fixtures → Israel's court. Onkelos's counting verb (u-le-mimnei, 'to count by them') and Targum Jonathan's molad ('birth of the moon') curriculum witness the same reading at translation level.
claims.middah_note: plain tannaitic prooftext derivation (she-ne'emar, 'as it is stated'); law-adjacent content in a narrative span
claims.mechanics: the TRIPLE's job-list criteria gain the delegated-duty annotation; NEW EXPORT (EXPORT_second_handover: divide handed machine→fixtures at 1:14, count handed fixtures→Israel per the tannaitic reading). Operator itself unchanged.

Confirms the v1 reading of the THEN-chain as a job assignment to the plural product; no tension with C1 (illumination is sun-only, calendar sanctification is moon-led, festival-fixing is joint).

claims.claim_en: SPEC DELTA #1 (ha-gedolim 'the great ones' → ha-gadol/ha-qaton 'the great/the small') is answered by the chain as a RECORDED DISPUTE over provenance with a converged outcome: reading A (Bavli) — created equal; the moon objected 'can two kings serve with one crown?' and was told 'go diminish yourself'; reading B (Bereshit Rabbah) — the chain asks our delta verbatim ('after He calls them GREAT, He turns and diminishes them?!') and answers: one entered its fellow's domain. (An anthology harmonization — great RELATIVE TO THE STARS — sits at enrichment tier, noted not elevated.) Both readings converge on the delivered state (one great, one small); they differ only on how the split happened.
claims.middah_note: carried open under the third-verse discipline (I13/E15 shape: two witnesses stand until a third decides; no deciding verse is recorded, so the dispute STANDS as machloket, never decided by the machine)

claims.claim_en: THE STANDING ATONEMENT LIABILITY: R. Pinchas — the New-Moon goat is written 'a sin offering FOR the Lord' (Num 28:15): 'bring an atonement FOR ME, for having diminished the moon.' The diminution settlement creates a RECURRING MONTHLY OBLIGATION that later Torah text refers to mechanically — the exact criterion of the owner's hidden-light ruling (2026-08-20): if later text refers to it, it must be in the world.
claims.middah_note: derivation from the anomalous phrase la-Adonai ('FOR the Lord') in Num 28:15 — a diqduq (close-reading) of a later verse applied back; plain-statement class in this span

claims.claim_en: THE COMPENSATIONS PACKAGE re-derives the calendar office as restitution: the diminished moon receives (a) rule by day AND night ('what use is a candle at noon?' — its daytime visibility), (b) Israel's count — 'let Israel COUNT the days and years with you', with our own 1:14 quoted back ('impossible they will not count seasons with the sun — ve-hayu le-otot u-le-mo'adim'), (c) the righteous named after the qatan ('the small one'). Ties C1 and C6: the calendar thesis and the diminution narrative are one settlement — the moon's office EXISTS as compensation. Confirms the v1 ASSIGN structure (offices, not names).
claims.middah_note: dialectical narrative (objection-and-compensation exchange); no numbered rule
claims.mechanics: evidence note on the ASSIGN operator; the C6 witness state carries the compensation clauses as its content. No new state.

claims.claim_en: THE HANDOVER READING OF THE INSTALL, machine-checkable in v2: the chain builds its objection from OUR verses — 'was light created on day one? but: va-yiten otam… yom revi'i (He set them… a fourth day, 1:17+1:19)!' — and resolves it with the hidden light: the day-one light was withdrawn and stored for the righteous, the day-4 fixtures installed as its OPERATING REPLACEMENT, with the deciding verse Ps 97:11 ('light is SOWN for the righteous'). Since the day-one canon amendment, WORLD_WITNESSED['hidden(or)'] exists in the world — so day 4's INSTALL can now READ it at witness tier: the handover is no longer a cross-reference in prose but a checkable state relation (fixtures mounted while the primordial light sits hidden). Bamidbar Rabbah's 'sparks of the supernal light' feeding the lamps (enrichment, row 2) supports the same dossier.
claims.middah_note: two passages contradict until a third text decides — the sugya itself supplies the deciding verse (Ps 97:11); the cleanest E15 instance in the corpus so far
claims.mechanics: the INSTALL step gains a witness-tier read: assert WORLD_WITNESSED contains hidden(or) (day-one v2 state) beside the mount — witness reads witness, the tier wall intact; Torah-tier registers untouched. This is the first cross-unit v2 integration.
